story.title: Senegal Restored as 2025 AFCON Champions Following CAS Ruling
story.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, overturning a previous decision that awarded the title to Morocco. The ruling confirmed Senegal's victory over Morocco in the final held in January, where Senegal won 1-0 after extra time. Morocco has expressed its intention to pursue further legal action in response to this decision.

explore_lenses.label: Why did CAS restore Senegal's victory?
explore_lenses.title: Referee restart was decisive
explore_lenses.summary: CAS treated the referee's decision to restart the final after Senegal's temporary walk-off as an on-field judgment, rather than a result that CAF could later replace through its forfeiture rules.

claims.text: The final was level after 90 minutes; Pape Gueye scored in the third minute of extra time as Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in Rabat on January 18, 2026.

CAS ruled that the referee alone had authority to decide whether play should resume, and that the referee's restart decision was protected by the field-of-play doctrine; it therefore confirmed the 1-0 result.
Morocco's federation argued that Senegal's temporary departure itself breached AFCON regulations and should have required the referee to end the match, making a 3-0 forfeiture appropriate.

Morocco's federation argued that Senegal's temporary departure itself breached AFCON regulations and should have required the referee to end the match, making a 3-0 forfeiture appropriate.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: CAS's media release is an official summary; it says the full written award has been issued to the parties and may be published publicly unless confidentiality is requested.

explore_lenses.label: Which consequences of the final still stand?
explore_lenses.title: Title restored, sanctions remain
explore_lenses.summary: The ruling reverses the title decision but does not erase the separate discipline imposed over the walk-off.

claims.text: CAS set aside CAF's March 17, 2026 Appeal Board decision and reinstated the CAF Disciplinary Board decision, restoring Senegal as AFCON 2025 winner.
CAS said CAF had already sanctioned the Senegalese federation, coach Pape Thiaw and certain players in separate disciplinary proceedings; those sanctions were not displaced by the title ruling.
CAF says it respects the CAS award and will take the measures needed to implement it.
The FRMF says it will pursue available legal remedies and has alleged an arbitrator's contact with the president of Senegal's federation affected the arbitration's integrity.

story_report.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champion, overturning a Confederation of African Football appeal decision that had declared Morocco the winner. The ruling confirmed Senegal’s 1-0 extra-time victory in the final and reinstated an earlier CAF disciplinary decision. CAF said it respects the award and will take the measures needed to implement it, while Morocco’s federation said it intends to pursue available legal remedies.

sections.heading: Senegal’s Extra-Time Final Victory
sections.body: The final in Rabat was scoreless after 90 minutes before Pape Gueye scored in the third minute of extra time, giving Senegal a 1-0 win over Morocco on January 18, 2026. CAS confirmed that result after examining the dispute over the match’s temporary interruption and subsequent restart.

sections.heading: Morocco’s Forfeiture Argument Rejected
sections.body: Morocco’s football federation argued that Senegal’s temporary departure from the field breached AFCON regulations and should have led the referee to end the match, resulting in a 3-0 forfeiture. CAS held that the referee alone had authority to decide whether play resumed and said the restart decision was protected by the field-of-play doctrine. It therefore set aside CAF’s March 17 Appeal Board decision and restored the prior disciplinary ruling in Senegal’s favour.

sections.heading: Existing Senegal Sanctions Remain
sections.body: CAS said separate disciplinary sanctions already imposed by CAF on the Senegalese federation, coach Pape Thiaw and certain players were not altered by its ruling on the title. CAF said it would implement the award, while the Moroccan federation has alleged that contact between an arbitrator and the president of Senegal’s federation affected the arbitration’s integrity.

unresolved.text: The official CAS materials supplied do not establish Morocco’s allegation concerning contact involving an arbitrator, and they do not say whether the Moroccan federation has filed a new court challenge. CAS said its full written award has been issued to the parties and may be published unless confidentiality is requested.

related_stories.title: Melania Trump Unveils 2026 White House Christmas Tree
related_stories.summary: First Lady Melania Trump welcomed the official 2026 White House Christmas tree in a ceremony on November 23, 2026. The tree, an 18-foot fir from Silent Night Evergreens in Wisconsin, arrived in a horse-drawn carriage, marking the beginning of the festive season at the White House.
